concepts.identity_authority: A local owner reference and scope root, not Source, account Profile, Artifact, or AI inference.
concepts.lifecycle: Created only by explicit local setup or migration; owner identity is never inferred from records; it may be deactivated only by an authorized account-level lifecycle outside this Fast Track.

core_mapping.Project: person is the owner/participant scope of a Project; Project remains independently identified.
core_mapping.Artifact: person may be author, recorder, or subject reference, while an Artifact keeps its own content identity.
core_mapping.Source: person owns or authorizes a Source but is never collapsed into the Source identity.
core_mapping.Assertion: person can assert or confirm a fact; an AI inference about a person remains an Assertion with AI identity.
core_mapping.Decision: person is the confirmer/decision-maker; decision rationale and evidence stay on Decision and Link.
core_mapping.Action: person can create, commit to, or confirm an Action; this does not make all Actions confirmed.
core_mapping.Event: person may be the affected subject or observer; Event retains occurrence versus capture time.
core_mapping.Derivation: person is a visible scope input, never an AI-generated profile payload or unbounded data grant.
core_mapping.Feedback: person is the explicit feedback actor; Feedback remains append-only and target-specific.
core_mapping.Authorization: person is the grantor/subject reference under six-dimensional authorization.
core_mapping.AuditEntry: person may be a scoped actor reference without writing identifying profile data into audit detail.
core_mapping.Link: person-related links retain source, confirmation, and validity; they do not grant processing access.

concepts.identity_authority: A controlled long-term life view and read-classification policy, not an App root, a permission scope shortcut, or a replacement for Project.
concepts.lifecycle: A domain may be configured as unenabled, enabled-for-reading, or deep-intelligence eligible only after separate data/value/feedback/safety gates; P3-128 creates none.

core_mapping.Project: a Project may be viewed through one or more Domains but retains Project recovery semantics.
core_mapping.Artifact: an Artifact can be tagged or linked to a Domain as a view; its source and content identity remain authoritative.
core_mapping.Source: a Source can be categorized for display but Domain never expands its read or processing authorization.
core_mapping.Assertion: a Domain can filter an Assertion for reading; it cannot convert a claim into a fact.
core_mapping.Decision: a Decision can be displayed in a Domain view without changing its Project/evidence links.
core_mapping.Action: an Action can be visible in a Domain view; confirmation and commitment stay Action/Feedback semantics.
core_mapping.Event: an Event may contribute to a Domain timeline without becoming a new domain-owned event type.
core_mapping.Derivation: a Domain is a declared processing/read scope in a Derivation constraint, never an implicit authorization.
core_mapping.Feedback: feedback about a Domain recommendation remains feedback on its concrete target and does not train a hidden person profile.
core_mapping.Authorization: a Domain may narrow a requested scope but cannot substitute for Source/Artifact/Project authorization.
core_mapping.AuditEntry: audit records the authorized operation and scope, not a broad Domain-derived data inventory.
core_mapping.Link: Domain links are typed views with confirmation/validity; a link cannot grant cross-domain access.

concepts.identity_authority: An application-level, Person-owned context container with stable ContextId; it is composed from existing core objects and is not a new core entity or database-table mandate.
concepts.lifecycle: candidate -> confirmed -> active -> watching -> closed; a Project-backed Context projects a Project lifecycle, while non-Project Contexts require explicit user confirmation before any durable creation.

core_mapping.Project: Project is the canonical backing object for context_type=project; ContextId is deterministically derived or explicitly linked, never a replacement Project.
core_mapping.Artifact: related Artifacts are evidence members selected through typed Links and current authorization checks.
core_mapping.Source: Context may display Sources through related evidence but does not own, read, or authorize them.
core_mapping.Assertion: current understanding includes Assertions with their confirmation/evidence status; it never treats them as Context fields of truth.
core_mapping.Decision: Context recovery shows confirmed or candidate Decisions with reasons and status.
core_mapping.Action: Context Next shows only Action role/status; an AI proposal remains candidate until Feedback confirms it.
core_mapping.Event: Context recent history is a projection of meaningful Events, preserving actual occurrence time.
core_mapping.Derivation: Context understanding is a Derivation-backed view and becomes unavailable/stale when its evidence or authorization fails.
core_mapping.Feedback: confirmation, correction, rejection, completion, and retraction are read from Feedback, not silently written by Context UI.
core_mapping.Authorization: every Context read and optional Resolver input is rechecked against current Authorization and source/evidence state.
core_mapping.AuditEntry: Context read, candidate confirmation, and authorized consumption are audit-worthy actions with minimized scoped references.
core_mapping.Link: typed Links bind Context backing objects and evidence; candidates remain visibly candidate and cannot expand permissions.

concepts.identity_authority: A long-term evidence and understanding read model, not a parallel authoritative original-content store or a new core object.
concepts.lifecycle: A MemoryItem is materialized from current core objects; it becomes stale, unavailable, or hidden when provenance, tombstone, source, evidence, or authorization checks fail, and is rebuildable from remaining lawful inputs.

core_mapping.Project: Memory can index Project recovery context but Project remains the recovery boundary.
core_mapping.Artifact: original and external content are displayed by reference to Artifact/version; Memory never copies them as its own authority.
core_mapping.Source: Memory exposes Source identity and availability for every evidence-bearing item.
core_mapping.Assertion: confirmed facts, external claims, and AI inferences stay distinct Assertion identities in the read model.
core_mapping.Decision: Memory answers why by prioritizing Decision, rationale, and linked original evidence.
core_mapping.Action: Memory may expose an Action history but never turns a proposal into a commitment.
core_mapping.Event: Memory timeline entries reference Events with their correct occurrence/capture semantics.
core_mapping.Derivation: all AI understanding, observation, inference, summary, or index entry points back to Derivation and exact inputs.
core_mapping.Feedback: confirmation/correction/retraction is rendered from Feedback history and current effect, never overwritten as text.
core_mapping.Authorization: every Memory query and detail projection rechecks authorization, purpose, location, and active-use eligibility.
core_mapping.AuditEntry: Memory consumption yields minimum audit metadata when required; audit is not a Memory data source.
core_mapping.Link: Memory traversal uses typed Links with provenance, confirmation, and validity to form an evidence graph.

concepts.identity_authority: An ephemeral request-scoped resolver result consisting of Person Context + Page Context + Selection Context, not a persisted profile, authority, or Agent task.
concepts.lifecycle: assembled on each request -> shown for review/removal -> authorization rechecked -> consumed or refused -> discarded; no component becomes durable merely by appearing in the resolver.

core_mapping.Project: Page/selection may reference a Project-backed Context only after current read authorization.
core_mapping.Artifact: selected Artifact versions are explicit resolver references and cannot be replaced by summaries.
core_mapping.Source: each resolver reference includes source availability/permission state; no hidden source expansion is allowed.
core_mapping.Assertion: Assertions enter only with identity and confirmation state visible to the user.
core_mapping.Decision: a Decision can be included as evidence; the resolver cannot confirm or alter it.
core_mapping.Action: an Action may be displayed as confirmed or candidate; AI cannot change its state through context assembly.
core_mapping.Event: Events are bounded page/selection evidence with correct temporal identity.
core_mapping.Derivation: any AI output must record this exact resolver input set as a new Derivation, never a durable global memory by default.
core_mapping.Feedback: Feedback can constrain what remains effective, but the resolver cannot fabricate feedback.
core_mapping.Authorization: every included ref is checked for subject, scope, action, purpose, location, and time; unknown/ambiguous denies.
core_mapping.AuditEntry: resolver assembly and authorized model consumption require minimized audit correlation, not raw content logging.
core_mapping.Link: Links may supply related evidence only when typed, valid, confirmed as required, and independently authorized.
